newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1997 exports seen growing 6.5 pct - DIHT.
newsitem.headline: German 1997 exports seen growing 6.5 pct - DIHT.

text.p: Germany's share of world markets is likely to continue its decline this year, despite faster export growth and a bigger trade surplus, the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce (DIHT) said on Thursday.

The lower value of the mark against the dollar and key European currencies will help exporters, but they won't be able to keep pace with growth in world trade, which is seen at eight percent, DIHT said, based on a survey of member chambers that specialise in foreign trade.
German exports are likely to grow 6.5 percent this year, up from 4.6 percent growth in 1996, while imports are likely to grow 4.5 percent, up from 3.1 percent, DIHT said.
The world economy is expected to grow 2.9 percent this year, and 3.2 percent next year, DIHT said.
In remarks prepared for delivery to journalists, DIHT manager Franz Schoser said most German companies had improved their competitiveness, and that key German export markets were seeing good growth.
German wage costs, while high, are rising more slowly than in other countries, but Germany's very high non-wage labour costs remain a burden for exporters, Schoser said.
German exports to other European countries are likely to grow less than the average at about five percent, but growth in other regions will more than compensate.
Exports to central and eastern Europe are seen growing 9.5 percent, and those to Asia and Africa nine percent.
Exports to North America should grow 8.5 percent, to the Middle East 7.5 percent, and to Latin America seven percent.
